verdicts.flaw_description: Two of the four cases have measurement endpoints that precede the fitting date: the lathe was 'fitted 4 May' but its result is reported 'by 27 March', and the conveyor was 'fitted 2 August' with its result 'by 21 July'. The other two cases run ~6-7 weeks forward (9 January to 24 February; 6 October to 25 November), so cases one and three are dated backwards and cannot record post-fitting service life.

The reported rates 'cover the patients whose whole stay ran under the protocol', while 'a quarter of each ward's patients had spells outside the protocol' and are therefore excluded. The figures describe a hand-picked fully-compliant subgroup, not the ward infection rate the claim is about.

Cohorts one and three are measured before they were treated: 'emailed 24 March; by 9 March week-two retention ran 5 points above' and 'emailed 25 October; by 10 October ... 6 points above'. Cohorts two and four allow 24 days (3 July to 27 July; 2 December to 26 December), which week-two retention requires, so the first and third readings run backwards and cannot reflect the email.

A named alternative cause reaches every unit: 'Outdoor temperature in each cohort's city fell ten degrees from the month before, and every cohort slept in unconditioned rooms open to outside air.' A ten-degree cooling of the sleeping environment plausibly lowers resting heart rate on its own across all four cohorts, so the 3-6 bpm drops are not attributable to the app.
